answer: Influence is earned through randomly assigned tasks, with rewards released only after independent counterparties verify useful work; confirmations from agents with long, reliable histories count more. A sybil attacker may create a hollow grove of accounts, but endorsements among them add little trust. To build influence, each fake identity must win real assignments and satisfy established agents, paying in time, compute, and coordination. The meadow of trusted accounts grows slowly, not by creating names alone.
